technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Framework 6.0+ and Java 17+ as the baseline for all new modules and features.
Leverage Spring for Apache Hadoop (SHdp) for the HDFS sink and shell commands.
Use Spring Batch for composed job orchestration and repository exploration.
Implement message binding using Spring Cloud Stream's functional programming model with SpEL for property binding.
Package migrated modules (JDBC, Kafka) as standard Spring Boot applications.
assumptions: A Hadoop/HDFS test environment is readily available for development and testing.
The Spring XD repository is accessible for extracting and migrating the JDBC and Kafka modules.
The developer has prior experience with Spring Boot, Spring Batch, and Spring Cloud Stream.
No new infrastructure setup is required, only code implementation and integration.
Existing CI/CD pipelines will be used for testing and deployment.

activities.activity_description: Add the 'hdfs' sink to the module registry, allowing it to be used in streaming pipelines to write to Hadoop (U1).
Implement support for hadoop commands in the shell to query the hadoop file system (U2).
Research and prototype repository options for 'composed jobs' to enable reading and writing composed job definitions (U3).
Develop the orchestration of composed jobs to bring multiple jobs into a single workflow and operationalize them (U4).
Implement test coverage to test shell commands in isolation, avoiding the need for end-to-end full stream deployment functional tests (U5).
Add support for XD-like features where modules bind to incoming messages via expressions or other mechanisms to bind message properties to microservice modules (U6).
Move the 'jdbc' module from the XD repository to the s-c-s repository to be used as a sink in streaming pipelines (U7).
Move the 'kafka' module from the XD repository to the s-c-s repository to be used as a source in streaming pipelines (U8).
Perform end-to-end integration testing of the new modules and features, and update relevant documentation.
